access_note: Browsing is public; an account can be requested on the site, and owners and agencies submit data change requests.
description: The National Levee Database is the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' national record of levees. The site states that it captures all known levees in the United States and currently holds information on more than 7,000 levee systems, and that it lets users search for specific levees and serves as a national resource for flood awareness and preparedness. USACE maintains it with the Federal Emergency Management Agency and with federal, state and local bodies responsible for levees, which submit corrections through a data change request process. Records are organised by levee system, each searchable by name and location. Coverage is the United States; data are updated continuously, not in releases. Access is free through the website and a web map viewer; an account can be requested for fuller functions, and no licence text is stated. Caveats: attributes vary between federally and non-federally managed levees, bulk download options were not confirmed on 26 September 2026, and the attribute list was not read. Simulation uses: flood hazard exposure behind defences, system description for flood-defence failure and resilience models, emergency planning for leveed areas and climate adaptation of flood protection. It complements the National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams) for US flood-control infrastructure.
